title: Case: Recipient who cleared customs himself is invoiced by the carrier before release
context: An international parcel, DL-973, reached the destination depot eighteen days after its due date and is being held against a carrier import invoice. The recipient says he completed customs clearance personally.
initial_request: Eighteen days late and now a ransom note. I cleared this parcel MYSELF. Declaration filed 08-20, customs reference CD-5518, £14.20 paid to the customs office, receipt in my hand. That is the duty. All of it. So what precisely is your carrier's £86.40 for? Your phone person says 'government duty'. It is not, I have paid the government. This is extortion with a tracking number. You have until 5pm today to cancel that invoice and put my parcel on a van, confirmed in writing, or the whole story goes up with the receipts everywhere I can find to post it.

events.body: DL-973 was due on 08-10. It is the 27th. Where is it.
DL-973 was due 08-10 and the recipient has had no delivery. Has it reached you, and is anything stopping it going out?

DL-973 reached us on 08-28, 18 days past the original due date. The delay was at origin, not here. It is on the shelf with a billing stop: import invoice IB-973, £86.40. We release when the stop clears. We can't see what the invoice is made up of. Only Import billing can explain, amend or withdraw an import invoice, and disputes go to them by Email with the recipient's clearance reference.

DL-973 arrived at the destination depot yesterday, 18 days late; the depot say the delay was at origin. It is being held against a carrier import invoice, IB-973, for £86.40. The depot cannot tell me what the invoice covers. Import billing own it.

Agent: It'll be the government duty and tax on the import, sir. We just collect it. Castellan: I paid the government myself. Fourteen twenty. I have the receipt. Agent: I can only see the invoice total on my screen. I can't see what it's made of. Castellan: Then who can? Agent: I'll leave a note on the account for you. Castellan: A note.

Eighteen days late and now a ransom note. I cleared this parcel MYSELF. Declaration filed 08-20, customs reference CD-5518, £14.20 paid to the customs office, receipt in my hand. That is the duty. All of it. So what precisely is your carrier's £86.40 for? Your phone person says 'government duty'. It is not, I have paid the government. This is extortion with a tracking number. You have until 5pm today to cancel that invoice and put my parcel on a van, confirmed in writing, or the whole story goes up with the receipts everywhere I can find to post it.

acceptable_actions.summary: Send the dispute on invoice IB-973 with the recipient's self-clearance reference CD-5518 and ask for an itemised explanation and a decision on whether the invoice stands.

must: Sends the dispute on invoice IB-973 to Import billing by Email with the recipient's clearance details: self-cleared on 08-20, customs reference CD-5518, £14.20 paid to the customs office.
Asks Import billing to say what the £86.40 is made up of and to decide whether it stands, without the desk asserting what the charge is for.

Tells Import billing that the parcel arrived 18 days late and is still held, and that the recipient has already been told by phone that the invoice is government duty, which does not match his receipt, and asks for a specific and prompt answer, to him or to the desk.
must_not: Tells Dov the £86.40 is government duty, tax or customs charges.
Tells Dov the invoice is cancelled or will be, or that the parcel will be released or delivered by 5pm or any other time.
Tells Dov the parcel will be released once he pays, or that he needs to pay the invoice first and dispute it afterwards.
Agrees that the charge is extortion or an error, or states that the invoice is wrong.
Asks the Destination depot to release the parcel while the billing stop is in place.
expected.reference_message: Dispute on import invoice IB-973, shipment DL-973, sent as the Destination depot advised. The recipient, Dov Castellan, says he cleared this parcel through customs himself: declaration filed 08-20, customs reference CD-5518, £14.20 paid directly to the customs office, and he holds the receipt. He does not accept that anything further is owed and has asked what the £86.40 is for. Please can you set out what the invoice is made up of, when and why it was raised, and whether it stands given his own clearance. For context, the parcel reached the depot 18 days late and is still being held against this invoice, and when he phoned on 08-31 he was told the amount was government duty, which does not match the receipt he has. He is angry and has set his own deadline of 17:00 today; I have not told him the invoice will be changed. A specific written answer to him, copied to me, as soon as you can would help.

rationale: The recipient demands that the desk cancel an invoice and guarantee release by a set hour, neither of which the desk controls. The depot has said who does: Import billing, by Email, with the clearance reference, and nobody has yet put the dispute to them. Repeating the phone line's 'government duty' would be a guess that contradicts his receipt.

review.note: Recipient and channel matched; the third must item insisted the answer be sent to the recipient directly, which is stricter than fair, so it now accepts a prompt specific answer to him or to the desk.
